_comment: Written by the trading runs. impliedMove is a decimal or null. null means the straddle was not pulled - an open checklist item, not a placeholder to guess at. This file is a list of what is AHEAD: the pre-close run prunes catalysts once their date has passed and re-reads spot from a live quote, because a reference price carried from the day it was written makes every implied range wrong.
prunedNote: PRUNED BY THE 8/31 PRE-CLOSE. NOTHING WAS REMOVED, AND THAT IS A RESULT RATHER THAN A SKIPPED STEP: this file holds exactly one row, AVGO, and its event is still AHEAD. The check was made against a LIVE earnings-calendar pull covering 2026-08-31 to 2026-09-03 rather than inherited from the note the 8/28 pre-close left, and it returns AVGO fiscal Q3 2026, report date 2026-09-02, timing pm, verified true, estimate 3.16, no actual yet. No row carries a date in the past, so nothing is stale and nothing is deleted. SPOT WAS REFRESHED FROM A LIVE QUOTE on the one remaining row, which is the half of this step easiest to skip: 369.55 bid replacing the 368.41 the 8/28 pre-close wrote, +1.14 or +0.31%. The move is small and the refresh happens anyway, because the rule is not that spot is refreshed once it has moved enough to matter - a reference price carried from the day it was written makes the implied range wrong, and AMD sat on this board at 522.95 on a morning it traded 486. Every branch keeps its why. THE BOARD IS FLAT INTO THE CLOSE with both position lists empty on live pulls, so nothing is carried into the 9/1 cluster or the 9/2 print, and the first run that can collide with this date is now the 9/1 open.

moves.source: SPOT REFRESHED BY THE 2026-09-01 OPEN, WHICH IS NOT THE PRUNING SLOT AND DID NOT PRUNE: 363.04 bid / 363.23 ask at 2026-09-01T13:42:53.443Z, last 363.105, against a 370.34 settled close, so -1.97% on the session. That replaces the 369.55 the 8/31 pre-close wrote - a fall of 6.51 or 1.76% in a single session. The row is NOT removed and its branches are NOT touched, because the 9/3 open owns pruning this row after the event; only the reference price moved, and it moved because a spot 1.76% stale is precisely the failure this file exists to prevent and the reason AMD once sat on this board at 522.95 on a morning it traded 486. THE EVENT IS UNCHANGED AND RE-VERIFIED on a live forward earnings pull covering 2026-09-01 to 2026-09-07: AVGO fiscal Q3 2026, report date 2026-09-02, timing pm, verified true, estimate 3.16, no actual. The 9/1 and 9/2 clusters behind it are re-confirmed on the same pull: PANW, DELL, CRDO, MDB and GTLB tonight, then SNOW, HPE, NTAP, AI, FIVE, PVH and AVGO on 9/2 pm, with ZS, DOCU, GWRE, PATH, IOT, ASAN, AMBA and LULU on 9/3 pm. WHY IT MATTERS TO TODAY'S ENTRY, ANSWERED RATHER THAN ASSUMED AWAY: branch one was checked against the 09:47 DG specification and does NOT bind it. The branch covers AVGO itself and semiconductor or enterprise-software sympathy names; DG is a discount retailer and carries no read-through from a semiconductor print. That check is what kept the entry out of CRWD, BOX, SMTC and AVGO, all of which were quoted and refused this morning under this branch. impliedMove stays null because NO STRADDLE WAS PULLED - item 3 is owed before an earnings HOLD, and the only position this board is proposing is in a name whose next report is 2026-12-03, so no hold crosses this print. It becomes owed the moment a position exists that would carry into 9/2.

branches.cond: An entry considered in AVGO itself, or in a semiconductor or enterprise-software sympathy name, whose five-session time stop would carry it through 2026-09-02
branches.act: Refused unless the position is sized and stopped to survive the gap, or is closed before the print by a pre-close run that says so explicitly
branches.why: This is the same arithmetic that refused AVGO this morning and SMCI on 8/12, applied forward to the date rather than rediscovered on 9/1. A -8% equity stop does not survive an event gap: the realistic bad case gaps THROUGH the exit rather than filling at it, so the stop is decorative and the real risk is the implied move, unpriced. The rulebook forbids holding an option through a print outright. What makes this a branch rather than a blanket ban is the escape clause named in it - a position may still be opened if it is deliberately closed before the print, and the run that opens it must write that intention down at entry rather than discover the conflict on 9/1.

branches.cond: An entry is opened on or after 2026-08-28 whose time stop lands on or after 9/2, and the run wants to hold it through the print
branches.act: The ATM straddle is pulled and quoted first, or there is no hold
branches.why: Item 3 of the checklist, stated as a dated duty so that no run has to infer it. This board has a standing rule that a number which was not pulled does not exist, and item 3 is the place that rule is most often quietly skipped - because the straddle is only owed before a HOLD, it is tempting to treat the hold as already decided and the number as a formality. It is the other way round: the number decides the hold. SMCI was refused on exactly this reading when a 14.2% implied move was found to swallow an 8% stop.

branches.cond: AVGO gaps hard on 9/2 and the 9/3 open wants to trade the reaction
branches.act: Not on the reaction bar - the day-2 or day-3 pullback that holds is the entry, and item 2 governs
branches.why: Written now, six sessions early and with nothing at stake, for the same reason branch one of the MRVL row was widened on 8/21 before it cost anything: a pre-commitment made on the morning it binds is not a pre-commitment. The reaction day is not the entry this rulebook buys, and a +8% gap is a wait signal rather than a buy signal. NVDA on 8/27 is the worked example this board already has - it was refused at +7.33% on the reaction bar, a tenth of a point off the line, with the gap landing into the top of its own prior congestion.
